title: Towards Empowering Stakeholders through Decentralized Trust and Secure Livestock Data Sharing
content: Cybersecurity presents a key challenge in data-sharing platforms involving multiple stakeholders, particularly in complex, decentralized systems such as livestock supply chain networks. Such systems require novel approaches, robust security protocols, and advanced data management solutions to address challenges such as data consistency, transparency, ownership, controlled exposure, and privacy-preserving analysis for value-added services. In this paper, we presented the Framework for Livestock Empowerment and Decentralized Secure Data eXchange (FLEX) framework, which is designed based on five core principles: (i) enhanced security and privacy, (ii) human-centric approach, (iii) decentralized and trusted infrastructure, (iv) system resilience, and (v) seamlesscollaboration across the supply chain. The framework integrates interdisciplinary innovations, where decentralized, infrastructure-based protocols facilitate trust, traceability, and integrity. It employs secure data-sharing protocols and cryptographic mechanisms to enable controlled information exchange with authorized parties. Additionally, the use of data anonymization techniques ensures privacy. FLEX was designed and developed using a microservices architecture and edge computing to support modularity and scalable platform deployment. All these components can be used as a foundational pillars of the digital product passport. The FLEX architecture is constructed using a layered design and incorporates robust security controls to address threats identified using the STRIDE threat model. The evaluation results demonstrate that the framework effectively mitigates well-known attacks while achieving the objectives described. Performance evaluation of the implementation further confirms its feasibility and showed its stability as the number of evidence added to animal identity. Furthermore, all infrastructure components, along with deployment instructions, are made available as open source libraries on github for public benefit
